businessRules.rule: An expulsion is recommended from a recorded incident, setting out what happened, what sanctions were already applied and why they were not sufficient. A case that does not show what was tried first is a case that has not been made.
Where the student has an open special educational need or safeguarding record, that record is reviewed before the case proceeds.
The guardian is informed of the case in writing and is heard. The meeting, who attended, and the family's response are recorded. This step is not optional and the case cannot proceed without it.

The Principal decides, and the decision and its reasons are recorded. Where the decision is not to expel, any lesser sanction applied instead is recorded against the same case, so a case that ended in something short of expulsion is still a case with an outcome.
The decision is the Principal's and is not configurable to a lower role.

An appeal window runs before the decision takes effect, its length set by the school. The appeal, if made, and its outcome are recorded. A decision that takes effect before a family can appeal it has no appeal.

On the decision taking effect, the leaving date is set and the enrolment closes. The student is removed from the section roster so class counts and teacher lists are correct, attendance stops being expected, alerts stop, and no further invoice is raised.
Accounts settle the fee position. Any unused credit and any security deposit held are refunded, and school property is returned — the ID card, library books and any equipment issued.

Any outstanding balance is chased or written off under the write-off use case by the approver named there, and is not approved within this one. An expulsion must not become a route around that control.

Which certificates are issued is decided explicitly by the Principal and recorded, rather than following automatically. The school leaving certificate is effectively required for the child to enrol anywhere else, so withholding it is a decision of a different order from withholding one over unpaid fees, and it is taken deliberately or not at all.
The record is set to Expelled and deactivated. It is never deleted, since results, the fee ledger, ledger entries and audit trails reference it.
A record closed on a disciplinary decision is flagged, so that any future admission attempt surfaces it rather than the school re-admitting the student unknowingly.
The whole case is written to the audit log with each step, its date and the person who took it.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Student → Expulsion cases → Recommend an expulsion
basicFlow.userAction: Recommends the expulsion from the incident record, setting out what happened, what sanctions were already applied and why they were not sufficient.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires all three, since a case that does not show what was tried first has not been made.

basicFlow.navigation: Expulsion cases → The decision → Review the support record
basicFlow.userAction: Reviews any open special educational need or safeguarding record before the case proceeds.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the review, and blocks the case until it is done where such a record exists.

basicFlow.userAction: Informs the family of the case in writing, hears them, and records the meeting, who attended and the family's response.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses to let the case proceed without it. This step is not optional.

basicFlow.userAction: Decides, and records the decision and its reasons.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records a lesser sanction against the same case where the decision is not to expel.
Runs the appeal window before the decision takes effect, and records any appeal and its outcome.

basicFlow.userAction: Sets the leaving date and closes the enrolment.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Removes the student from the section roster, stops attendance being expected, stops the alerts and raises no further invoice.

basicFlow.navigation: Clearance and settlement → Settle fees, Refund credit, Refund deposit, Record property returned
basicFlow.userAction: Settles the fee position, refunds any unused credit and any security deposit, and records school property returned.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records each item, and refuses a write-off raised from within this case.

basicFlow.navigation: The decision → Decide which certificates are issued
basicFlow.userAction: Decides explicitly which certificates are issued and records that decision.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Raises a request only for the certificates decided, and sets the record to Expelled, deactivated and flagged.

departures.requirement: There is no route by which a decision is recorded before the family has been informed in writing and heard, and the meeting recorded. This step is not optional and the case cannot proceed without it.
The decision cannot take effect and the enrolment cannot close until the window has run. A decision that takes effect before a family can appeal it has no appeal.

No certificate is issued or withheld automatically. The Principal decides explicitly and the decision is recorded, because the leaving certificate is effectively required for the child to enrol anywhere else.

departures.requirement: A balance cannot be written off from within this case. The write-off has its own approver and this must not become a way past it.
A record closed on a disciplinary decision is flagged so any future admission attempt surfaces it. The school must not re-admit unknowingly.
The case and every step of it are retained 7 years or longer, since this is the most consequential action the school takes against a child and may be questioned years later.

openQuestions.question: How long is the appeal window? The document says the school sets it and does not state a length.
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and nothing can take effect without it.

openQuestions.question: Who hears an appeal — the Principal who made the decision, or somebody else?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. An appeal heard by the decision-maker is not much of an appeal.

openQuestions.question: Does a flagged record bar re-admission outright, or only surface at the attempt?
Must the family be offered the chance to bring somebody with them to the hearing?
Is the student heard as well as the guardian, and is that recorded separately?
openQuestions.assumption: Who attended is recorded, but the student's own account is not a separate field.

openQuestions.question: Where the decision is not to expel, does the lesser sanction go through its own approval, or is recording it here enough?
openQuestions.assumption: Recorded here as modelled. A suspension recorded this way would bypass its own approval.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
